title: Orphaned VMDK Files on Datastores
exclusions: Surfaces review candidates produced by a complete, qualified datastore-file versus vCenter-reference snapshot; it does not prove that a VMDK is orphaned or safe to delete. The contract is limited to explicitly approved VMFS or NFS datastores whose browser and inventory scans both complete. It excludes vSAN object paths, vVols, inaccessible datastores, Content Library and image-service storage unless their references are integrated, active/registered VM disks, templates, snapshots and delta chains, linked clones, replication/backup products, First Class Disks/Improved Virtual Disks, pending imports/exports/clones/migrations, descriptor/extent pairs that cannot be resolved, change windows, lock/in-use checks, and ungoverned vCenters. File size is bytes and displayed as GiB (2^30 bytes), not decimal GB. Candidate age and 100 GiB severity are local review policies, not VMware defaults. Missing or partial snapshots are health failures. The search performs no datastore browse beyond the source event and never deletes, renames, moves, opens, consolidates, or repairs a disk.
evidence: After deployment retain authoritative vCenter, datastore type, ownership, backup/replication, Content Library, FCD, template, snapshot, and active-change inventory; collector code/hash and allowlist; vCenter/ESXi/VCF PowerCLI/Splunk versions; datastore browse and inventory privileges; effective scripted-input/JSON configuration; complete manifest and reference-set hashes/counts; raw candidate rows and collector errors; expected-datastore, completeness, schema, age, duplicate, and freshness health; `vmware_unreferenced_vmdk_candidates` definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, results, alert delivery, analyst two-person review, live recheck, storage-owner disposition, and any separately approved cleanup record. Preserve vCenter, datacenter, datastore/moid/type, canonical path, descriptor/extent identity, bytes, modification epoch, reason, reference-manifest ID, snapshot ID/epoch, exclusions checked, and source health. These prove only that the documented comparison produced a candidate. This documentation-only review created no scan, event, candidate, lock test, deletion, capacity recovery, or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Build a fixed complete fixture for one approved VMFS datastore. Include an unreferenced descriptor VMDK of 107374182400 bytes last modified eight days before the fixed search time, with its extent chain resolved and no active-change marker. Expect one `review_required` row at exactly 100.000 GiB and local high severity. Include a second 1073741824-byte candidate older than seven days and expect 1.000 GiB, medium severity. Assert canonical identity, bytes-to-GiB conversion, age, snapshot/reference IDs, and UC ID.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for a file referenced by any registered VM/template/snapshot/FCD/approved Content Library manifest; a delta or extent whose descriptor/chain is referenced; a candidate seven days old or younger; a partial/failed file or reference scan; unsupported datastore type; active change window; blank identity; nonnumeric/negative size or epochs; stale/future snapshot; superseded older candidate; and duplicate delivery. Separate health controls must expose an expected datastore absent from the snapshot, unresolved descriptor chain, excluded reference domain, scan error, and stale manifest.

dataSources: A reviewed VCF PowerCLI/vSphere API collector uses `HostDatastoreBrowser.SearchDatastoreSubFolders_Task` with `Datastore.Browse` to enumerate VMDK metadata on an explicit datastore allowlist, and independently builds a canonical reference set from all governed VM/template hardware, snapshots, FCDs, Content Libraries, backup/replication registrations, and active tasks included in local scope. It emits only complete comparison candidates to deployment-local `index=vmware`, `sourcetype=vmware:unreferenced_vmdk_candidate`. Required fields include `vcenter`, `datacenter`, `datastore`, `datastore_moid`, `datastore_type`, `canonical_path`, `candidate_kind=descriptor`, integer `size_bytes`, `modified_epoch`, `candidate_reason=unreferenced_descriptor`, `chain_resolved=true`, `active_change=false`, integer `snapshot_epoch`, `snapshot_id`, `reference_manifest_id`, and `collector_status=ok`. This is not a native Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics source type.
app: A locally maintained and peer-reviewed `TA_vmware_storage_inventory` collector plus JSON source type, and a restricted Splunk app for source health, review search, dashboard, tests, and runbook. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (5089) can provide supporting datastore inventory/capacity but does not document orphan-file comparison.
spl:
index=vmware sourcetype="vmware:unreferenced_vmdk_candidate" collector_status="ok" candidate_reason="unreferenced_descriptor" candidate_kind="descriptor" chain_resolved="true" active_change="false" earliest=-10d
| eval vcenter=lower(trim(vcenter)), datastore=trim(datastore), datastore_moid=trim(datastore_moid), datastore_type=lower(trim(datastore_type)), canonical_path=trim(canonical_path), size_bytes=tonumber(size_bytes), modified_epoch=tonumber(modified_epoch), snapshot_epoch=tonumber(snapshot_epoch), snapshot_id=trim(snapshot_id), reference_manifest_id=trim(reference_manifest_id)
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(datastore)>0 AND len(datastore_moid)>0 AND len(canonical_path)>0 AND in(datastore_type,"vmfs","nfs","nfs41") AND size_bytes>=0 AND isnotnull(modified_epoch) AND isnotnull(snapshot_epoch) AND modified_epoch<=snapshot_epoch AND len(snapshot_id)>0 AND len(reference_manifest_id)>0
| sort 0 vcenter datastore_moid canonical_path -snapshot_epoch -_indextime
| dedup vcenter datastore_moid canonical_path
| eval snapshot_age_seconds=now()-snapshot_epoch, candidate_age_seconds=now()-modified_epoch
| where snapshot_age_seconds>=0 AND snapshot_age_seconds<=864000 AND candidate_age_seconds>604800
| eval size_gib=round(size_bytes/1073741824,3), candidate_age_days=floor(candidate_age_seconds/86400), local_severity=if(size_bytes>=107374182400,"high","medium"), finding="review_required", use_case="UC-2.1.34", modified_utc=strftime(modified_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), scanned_utc=strftime(snapshot_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table vcenter datacenter datastore datastore_moid datastore_type canonical_path size_bytes size_gib candidate_age_days modified_utc finding local_severity snapshot_id reference_manifest_id scanned_utc snapshot_age_seconds use_case
| sort 0 -size_bytes vcenter datastore canonical_path
description: Surfaces aged VMDK descriptor files that a qualified, complete collector could not match to any reference domain included in the same vCenter snapshot. The search preserves canonical path, exact bytes, binary GiB conversion, age, datastore identity, and manifest provenance and labels every row for human review rather than declaring a disk orphaned.
value: Unreferenced virtual-disk files can consume costly datastore capacity, but an unsafe deletion can destroy a VM, snapshot, template, replication target, or recovery asset. A conservative candidate workflow helps storage teams quantify possible waste while requiring fresh inventory, explicit exclusions, live revalidation, ownership, and approved cleanup before any destructive action.
implementation: Qualify a read-only weekly collector on an explicit VMFS/NFS allowlist, prove every reference domain and canonicalization rule, and reject partial scans. Save the aged-candidate search, independently monitor datastore/manifest completeness, validate exact byte/GiB boundaries and reference exclusions, then require storage-owner and two-person live recheck before a separate cleanup change. Never automate deletion from this result.
visualization: Use a restricted candidate table with datastore, canonical path, bytes, GiB, age, reason, manifest/snapshot, exclusions checked, owner, live-recheck status, and disposition. Add sums in GiB by datastore and age buckets plus separate unsupported-datastore, incomplete-scan, unresolved-chain, excluded-domain, and stale-snapshot panels. Label all totals `candidate capacity`, never `recoverable capacity`.
schema: Purpose-built complete datastore/reference comparison candidate JSON; no applicable CIM dataset
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. CIM does not represent canonical datastore-file identity, VMDK descriptor chains, reference-domain completeness, candidate provenance, or destructive-review state.

knownFalsePositives:
Every result is intentionally a candidate, not a deletion decision. Likely benign explanations include:

1. **Snapshot or delta-chain reference missed** — a descriptor, flat extent, delta, sesparse, or parent may be reachable indirectly. Reconstruct and validate the complete chain before any action.

2. **Template, Content Library, FCD, backup, or replication ownership** — products can retain files outside ordinary VM hardware enumeration. Confirm every locally scoped reference manifest and product owner.

3. **Active lifecycle task** — clone, Storage vMotion, import/export, restore, consolidation, or replication can temporarily create unreferenced-looking files. Correlate vCenter tasks/events and product jobs across the exact interval.

4. **Recently removed inventory object awaiting recovery decision** — an intentionally unregistered VM or failed registration can leave valid files. Search configuration/history and change records; do not equate unregistered with abandoned.

5. **Canonicalization defect** — escaped paths, datastore renames, case behavior, bracket notation, URL encoding, and multiple vCenters can break equality. Preserve native and canonical identities and test them per datastore type.

6. **Incomplete scan falsely marked complete** — permissions, timeout, inaccessible folders, API truncation, or task failure can reduce either set. Any count/hash anomaly invalidates the snapshot.

7. **Duplicate collector route** — repeated candidate events do not double physical bytes. The search deduplicates canonical identity within the newest snapshot, while health must remove duplicate delivery.

Suppress notification only for an exact canonical path and datastore identity with reason, owner, approved start, and finite expiry. Never suppress scan completeness, unresolved chains, excluded-domain warnings, or expected-datastore health.
mitreAttack: N/A (storage-capacity review; no adversary behavior asserted)
detectionType: Aged unreferenced VMDK descriptor candidate from complete set comparison
reviewer: Source-backed documentation-only editorial review; production VMware storage, backup, and Splunk validation pending

cost.search_load_notes: The Splunk search is small; datastore browsing and complete reference-set construction are the material vCenter/storage costs and must run off-peak.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and destructive-risk boundary

Assign VMware, storage, backup, replication, Content Library, application, Splunk, and change owners. Inventory vCenters and explicitly approved datastores by managed-object ID, type, accessibility, owner, maintenance window, backup/replication products, image libraries, FCD use, and retention obligations. Start only with lab and low-risk VMFS/NFS stores. Broadcom's datastore browser returns matching file metadata and requires Datastore.Browse; it does not tell you that a file is unused or safe to delete.

Define all reference domains before coding: registered VMs, templates, hardware backing paths, snapshot/delta parent chains, linked clones, FCDs, Content Libraries/image services, backup/replication ownership, active tasks, and intentionally unregistered recovery assets. If a domain cannot be enumerated, mark it excluded and do not claim complete orphan detection. Do not use this workflow for vSAN/vVol until their object semantics are separately designed.

## Step 1 — Build a complete comparison collector

Implement `TA_vmware_storage_inventory` on a hardened PowerCLI collection tier. Use `SearchDatastoreSubFolders_Task` with a VMDK file query and request file size and modification metadata. File metadata queries can still be expensive; serialize or cap concurrency, run off-peak, record task duration, and stop on timeout or API fault. Canonicalize bracket datastore paths and retain the native path.

In the same bounded run, build the full reference set. Resolve descriptors to extents and delta parents; never report an extent independently merely because its filename is absent from `Get-HardDisk`. Record a manifest hash/count per reference domain and active-task snapshot. Emit candidates only when both file and reference scans complete, chain resolution succeeds, datastore type is supported, no active-change marker applies, and the descriptor is absent from every included reference set. One shared `snapshot_id` and immutable `reference_manifest_id` must join evidence. Errors and partial results go to a separate health source.

Configure a weekly scripted input with explicit JSON source type and local index. Protect paths because names can disclose customers and applications. Compare file counts and several known paths with vSphere Client Datastore Browser and all owning products; do not use the UI alone as proof of nonuse.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save sidecar `spl` as `vmware_unreferenced_vmdk_candidates`. It accepts only successful, chain-resolved, inactive-change descriptor candidates from ten days, validates identity, supported type, exact byte and epoch fields, and newest snapshot per canonical path. Snapshot freshness is ten days because collection is weekly. Candidates must be strictly older than seven days. Bytes divide by 1,073,741,824 to display GiB; the raw byte count remains authoritative. Exactly 100 GiB receives local high routing, not a vendor severity. Every row says `review_required`.

Create independent health for expected datastores, collector status, per-domain manifest presence/count/hash, unresolved chains, unsupported types, run duration, task faults, snapshot age, duplicate routes, and event schema. A primary zero-row result is valid only when all included-domain health is green.

## Step 3 — Validate set logic and units

Use synthetic manifests covering descriptor plus flat extent, multi-extent disks, snapshots/deltas, linked clone parents, templates, FCDs, Content Library, backup/replication, active clone/migration, inaccessible folder, datastore rename, URL escaping, duplicate names across vCenters, zero-byte file, future modification, exactly seven days, exactly 100 GiB, partial scans, and duplicate delivery. Assert that any referenced chain yields no candidate and that bytes/GiB are exact.

In a lab, create a disposable VM/disk, snapshot, template, clone, unregistered VM, and governed unattached test descriptor. Compare collector output with API and Datastore Browser. Re-register the object and prove the candidate disappears on the next complete snapshot. Do not delete even lab candidates through the detection pipeline; exercise cleanup only in a separately approved test. Keep draft until every reference-domain owner signs scope and false-negative limitations.

## Step 4 — Review and respond safely

Route candidates to a queue, not an automated incident or cleanup. Reviewer sequence: verify raw event and snapshot health; rerun a fresh complete scan; inspect descriptor and full chain read-only; search vCenter inventory/tasks/events and all reference domains; identify datastore/path owner; verify backup/retention/legal requirements; test whether any host/process holds or accesses the file using supported tools; and obtain two-person VMware/storage approval with rollback before a separate move/quarantine or deletion change.

Never delete, rename, move, consolidate, attach, open for write, or modify a VMDK from this alert. Quarantine itself can break references. Close as referenced/retained, active task, collector defect, approved cleanup, or unresolved. Capacity is recovered only after storage reports it and workload/recovery validation passes; candidate GiB is not recovered GiB.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **Scan times out:** reduce datastore scope/concurrency, inspect vCenter task and storage latency, then mark the run partial; never publish its set difference.
- **Huge candidate surge:** suspect a missing reference domain, permission change, canonicalization regression, datastore rename, or collector version before storage waste.
- **Descriptor chain unresolved:** preserve all path metadata and remove it from the actionable set until a qualified parser/API resolves it.
- **Candidate exists in UI inventory:** compare native/canonical path, vCenter and datastore moid, snapshots, template/FCD/library ownership, and manifest hash.
- **Sizes differ:** file metadata is bytes; verify descriptor versus extent and sparse/provisioned semantics. Do not sum descriptor text size as disk capacity.
- **Duplicate totals:** deduplicate physical canonical path and inspect multiple collectors/vCenters; do not sum repeated observations.
- **File vanished:** verify approved task, retention, product cleanup, datastore accessibility, and audit history; disappearance alone does not prove safe reclamation.

Retention, age, and severity are local governance choices. This page documents candidate discovery, not deletion authorization.
grandmaExplanation: We look for old virtual-disk files that no known machine or approved storage service appears to use. Because deleting the wrong file could destroy data, every result is only a carefully documented review candidate.
hardware: Explicitly approved VMFS, NFS, or NFS 4.1 datastores visible through vCenter. vSAN, vVol, object/image-library, replication, and backup repositories remain out of scope until separately qualified.
